boixo-qa-hamiltonian-definition: Introduction, p.1, Eq. (3): the paper defines H(t) and the schedule conditions in one passage.
boixo-test-hamiltonian-17-fold: Main text, p.2: the paper states its own eight-qubit test Hamiltonian (Fig. 1) and its 17-fold ground state; Appendix C, p.8, derives the 16 plus 1 structure.
boixo-cluster-and-isolated-state: Main text, p.2, Eqs. (4a), (4b): the structure of the paper's own test Hamiltonian; the four-flip distance follows from the listed states and Appendix C, p.8.
boixo-definition-ps-pc: Main text, p.2: the paper defines pi, ps and the average cluster probability pC.
boixo-single-flip-connectivity-counts: Main text, p.2 and Appendix E, p.9: exact counting for the paper's own Hamiltonian. Each of the 8 single flips of the isolated state raises the energy from -8 to -4 (Eq. C1); a cluster state with l down ancillae reaches l energy -4 states and 4-l energy 0 states, so at most 4 excited neighbors. I rechecked it against Eq. (C1). Conclusion is exact, not an approximation.
boixo-master-equation-assumptions: Appendix A, p.5, Eq. (A6): the paper states the coupling form it assumes and what it neglects.
boixo-lamb-shift-ignored: Appendix A, p.5: the paper states that it ignores the Lamb shift in its model. The 'small perturbation' reason is the authors' stated reason, not a proved fact; Appendix G, p.11 shows the Lamb shift can matter in the SCL.
boixo-kms-detailed-balance: Appendix B, p.7, Eqs. (B1) to (B7): the paper states the KMS, analyticity in the strip and vanishing-at-infinity conditions and proves Eq. (A4) by a Cauchy-Goursat contour integral (a textbook tool). Continuity at the strip boundary is noted in the proof and cited to [34] as a property; it does not hide a cited theorem step.
boixo-experiment-device: Main text, p.3: the paper states its own device and qubit counts.
boixo-experiment-energy-scales: Main text, p.3: the paper states its own energy scales and temperature (10GHz, 5.3GHz, 17mK about 0.35GHz).
boixo-experiment-run-protocol: Main text, p.3: the paper states its own run protocol (144 embeddings, 4000 runs, batches of 1000).
boixo-fig4-annealing-time: Figure 4 caption, p.4: 'The total annealing time was T = 5 µs in each run'. The unit sits in the caption, as the value says.
boixo-control-precision: Main text, p.4: the paper states a limited control precision of about 5% in {hj, Jjk} as a limit of its own hardware. The reader typed it 'measured'; it is a hardware setup limit, not a measured result.
boixo-fig6-decoherence-time-sim: Figure 6 caption, p.6: the paper states a parameter of its own simulation (decoherence time 150ns).
boixo-scope-limit-no-speedup: Main text, p.4: the paper states that its study covers a non-classical signature and not computational speedup. It is a scope statement; the reader typed it 'measured', it should be 'scope'.
boixo-no-local-minima-proof: Appendix C, p.8: the claim and its argument are both in the paper. Flip all ancillae down (never raises energy by Eq. C1), then flip core spins to align them (core-ancilla pair energy does not rise, Eq. C1). I followed the argument and it is sound for the Hamiltonian of Fig. 1.
boixo-core-ancilla-pair-spectrum: Appendix C, p.8, Eq. (C1): the pair spectrum (-1, -1, 3, -1) is an exact calculation. I recomputed it from the Fig. 1 fields (+1 core, -1 ancilla) and coupling 1; it matches.
boixo-ground-state-energy: Appendix C, p.8: four pairs at -1 plus the aligned core ring at -4 give -8, derived from Eq. (C1) and the 4-2s core energy. The arithmetic checks.
boixo-sa-metropolis-rule: Appendix D, p.8, Eq. (D1): the paper states the update rule of its own simulations.
boixo-fig8-schedules-definition: Figure 8 caption, p.9: the paper defines the three schedules and their parameters.
boixo-appendix-e-slow-thermalization-ass: Appendix E, p.8: the paper states the regime its derivation covers (slow thermalization, similar populations of single-flip neighbors) and the plateau structure.
boixo-appendix-e-isolated-rate-equation: Appendix E, p.9, Eq. (E2): derived by counting the 8 single flips (4 core, 4 ancilla) from Eq. (A17) and (C1), with the equal-rate assumption stated. pe as one population rests on the slow-thermalization premise of the previous item.
boixo-appendix-e-cluster-counting: Appendix E, p.9: exact counting from the core-ancilla cases |up up> and |up down> using Eq. (C1); the derivation is in the passage.
boixo-appendix-e-cluster-assumption: Appendix E, p.9: the paper states the assumption of its own derivation ('we shall assume').
boixo-appendix-f-isolated-unconnected: Appendix F, p.10, Eqs. (F1) to (F4): first-order degenerate perturbation theory on the 17-dimensional ground subspace, with Htrans treated as the perturbation. The projected operator is exact for that order and shows the isolated state is not lowered. The result holds to first order only, which the 'perturbed' quote carries.
boixo-appendix-h-no-mid-anneal-measureme: Appendix H, p.11: the paper states that its device cannot measure during annealing, a limit of its own experiment. The reader typed it 'measured'; it should be 'scope'.

theory_low.boixo-classical-prediction-enhanced: Main text, p.2: a prediction ('As we show below'). Appendix E, p.8 to 10, argues it with approximate rate equations (E5) and a non-equilibrium ratio assumption, plus SA numerics. Not a proof.
theory_low.boixo-qa-prediction-suppressed: Main text, p.2: a prediction of open system QA. It rests on perturbation arguments and simulations (p.3), not a proof.
theory_low.boixo-sa-master-equation-derivation: Appendix A, p.4 to 6: the derivation starts from the Lindblad equation (A1), which the paper takes from its Ref. [21] ('We have previously established'), plus the rotating wave approximation, a chosen coupling form (A6) and a thermal-bath assumption. A proof that uses a specific other paper's result as a step is not a proved result. 'From first principles' overstates it.
theory_low.boixo-qa-prediction-longer-time-ps-incre: Main text, p.4: a prediction argued from thermal convergence and compared with a simulation (Fig. 6). Not proved here.
theory_low.boixo-qa-gap-lifts-degeneracy: Main text, p.3 with Fig. 2: a theoretical argument backed by simulated spectra (and first-order perturbation in Appendix F). The suppression claim is a prediction, not a proved theorem.
theory_low.boixo-qa-suppression-persists-four-flips: Main text, p.3: an argument about transitions that the paper says is 'confirmed by our simulations'. Not a proof.
theory_low.boixo-fig2-read-gap: Read from a figure (never HIGH on the figure alone). I checked the rendered page 3: the reading matches Fig. 2 (about 5.8 GHz at 0.3, about 2 GHz near 0.45, about 0 by 0.6, shoulder on the top curve near 0.45 to 0.5, B about 2.5 GHz at the right edge).
theory_low.boixo-16-fold-degeneracy-origin: Appendix C, p.8: the quoted sentence is cut before its states, and as printed it names |up up> and |down up> (a typo; the earlier sentence says core up with the ancilla up or down). The value gives the corrected reading, which the quotes do not carry. The physics is right, but the value says more than its quotes.
theory_low.boixo-appendix-e-cluster-approximation: Appendix E, p.10, Eq. (E5): an approximation. The paper drops the energy-0 terms by an informal argument ('for most temperatures of interest'), with no bound.
theory_low.boixo-appendix-e-ps-geq-pc: Appendix E, p.10, Eqs. (E5) to (E7): the argument uses the approximate cluster equation (E5) and a physical assumption that the excited to ground ratio is not below equilibrium ('will not be lower'), which is argued, not proved.
theory_low.boixo-appendix-f-sixth-excited-state: Appendix F, p.10: 'only the sixth excited state overlaps with the isolated state' is stated with no derivation. First-order theory (F4) gives the isolated state energy 0, degenerate with six cluster states, so it does not fix its level. Fig. 2 plots it, but the paper does not prove it.
theory_low.boixo-appendix-g-scl-agrees-classical: Appendix G, p.10 to 11: a derivation under limit assumptions (Markov, bath correlation time to zero, infinite temperature) whose agreement with classical thermalization is asserted, not shown. A claim about the authors' simulations.
theory_low.boixo-appendix-g-scl-predicts-enhancemen: Appendix G, p.11: the enhancement prediction is asserted from the SCL form, with no calculation shown, and the contradiction is with one device's data. A theoretical prediction plus a measured comparison.
theory_low.boixo-appendix-g-scl-computational-basis: Appendix G, p.11: an argued consequence of the SCL ('it predicts'), without a separate proof.
theory_low.boixo-appendix-h-concurrence-finite: Appendix H, p.11, Fig. 11: a simulation result, with an author inference ('This suggests') about the experiment, which the paper says it cannot test.
theory_low.boixo-fig11-read-concurrence: Read from a figure (never HIGH on the figure alone). I checked the rendered page 11: peaks near t/T 0.2 to 0.25 at about 0.14 (external edge, ground state) and about 0.10 (center edge, thermal), near 0 by 0.7. The reading matches.
